arXiv:1005.5070v1 [nlin.SI] 27 May 2010

Auto-Bäcklund Transformation for the r-th Double
Modified Dispersionless Kadomtsev–Petviashvili Equation

The work of the first author was partially supported by the joint grant 09-01-92438-KE_a of RFBR (Russia) and Consortium E.I.N.S.T.E.IN (Italy). The work of the second author was partially supported by the RFBR grant 08-01-00054-à and by the grant of Presidium of RAS ”Fundamental Problems of Nonlinear Dynamics”
Oleg I. Morozov Affiliation: of RAS, 53 Leninskii Ave., Moscow 119991, Russia    Maxim V. Pavlov Affiliation: M.V.Pavlov@lboro.ac.uk Affiliation: Sector of Mathematical Physics, P.N. Lebedev Physical Institute
Abstract

We find auto-Bäcklund transformation for the r-th double modified dispersionless Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation.

ams
58H05, 58J70, 35A30

The aim of this paper is to construct an auto-Bäcklund transformation for the r-th double modified dispersionless Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation

−κ⁡(uyux+uxκ+1)​ux​y\displaystyle-\kappa\,\left(\frac{u_{y}}{u_{x}}+u_{x}^{\kappa+1}\right)\,u_{xy}

with κ∉{−2,−3/2,−1}\kappa\not\in\{-2,-3/2,-1\}. This equation appears from the differential covering, [4, 5, 6],

ut\displaystyle u_{t} =\displaystyle= ((κ+2)22​κ+3​ux2​(κ+1)+(κ+2)​wx​uxκ+1+κ+12​wx2−wy)​ux,\displaystyle\left(\frac{(\kappa+2)^{2}}{2\,\kappa+3}\,u_{x}^{2(\kappa+1)}+(\kappa+2)\,w_{x}\,u_{x}^{\kappa+1}+\frac{\kappa+1}{2}\,w_{x}^{2}-w_{y}\right)u_{x}, (2)
uy\displaystyle u_{y} =\displaystyle= −(uxκ+1+wx)​ux\displaystyle-\left(u_{x}^{\kappa+1}+w_{x}\right)u_{x} (3)

over the r-th modified dispersionless Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation, [1],

wy​y=wt​x+(12​(κ+1)​wx2+wy)​wx​x+κ​wx​wx​y,w_{yy}=w_{tx}+\left({\textstyle\frac{1}{2}}\,(\kappa+1)\,w_{x}^{2}+w_{y}\right)\,w_{xx}+\kappa\,w_{x}\,w_{xy}, (4)

see [2], [3], [9], [8]. Namely, excluding ww from (2) and (3) yields Eq. (1).

Using the method of [7] we obtain the following

theorem : Equations

vt\displaystyle v_{t} =\displaystyle= (κ+2)22​κ+3​vx2​κ+3−(κ+2)​(uyux+uxκ+1)​vxκ+2\displaystyle\frac{(\kappa+2)^{2}}{2\kappa+3}\,v_{x}^{2\kappa+3}-(\kappa+2)\,\left(\frac{u_{y}}{u_{x}}+u_{x}^{\kappa+1}\right)\,v_{x}^{\kappa+2} (5)
+(utux+(κ+2)​uxκ​uy+(κ+1)​(κ+2)2​κ+3​ux2​κ+2)​vx,\displaystyle+\left(\frac{u_{t}}{u_{x}}+(\kappa+2)\,u_{x}^{\kappa}u_{y}+\frac{(\kappa+1)(\kappa+2)}{2\kappa+3}u_{x}^{2\kappa+2}\right)\,v_{x},
vy\displaystyle v_{y} =\displaystyle= −vxκ+2+(uyux+uxκ+1)​vx\displaystyle-v_{x}^{\kappa+2}+\left(\frac{u_{y}}{u_{x}}+u_{x}^{\kappa+1}\right)\,v_{x} (6)

define a covering for Eq. (1).

The covering (5), (6) has the following remarkable property — expressing utu_{t} and uyu_{y} from (5) and (6) gives the same result as the change of variables u↦vu\mapsto v, v↦uv\mapsto u. In other words, from (5) and (6) it follows that vv satisfies to Eq. (1). Therefore Eqs. (5) and (6) define an auto-Bäcklund transformation for Eq. (1).
